blocks.x: For nearly a decade my two sons and I have used more than 30 different kids’ water bottles. And since I started reviewing gear professionally, my “assistants” and I have officially tested nearly as many insulated and lightweight plastic options. I’m always quick to dismiss anything that’s complicated to clean, and they often uncover durability issues within a matter of days. Our combined criteria have left us with a pretty short short-list of reusable water bottles that are durable, dishwasher-safe, spillproof, and (save for the sippy-style Nalgene I recommend for toddlers) almost completely leakproof when properly closed.
My top picks

New in this review: My kids took a few new-to-us bottles back to school recently, which resulted in a new recommendation and a few more bottles to add to the laundry list of bottles we don’t recommend. I’ve also included the full list of the plastic and stainless-steel versions I’ve officially tested over the last few years, organized by dealbreaker.

The very best kids' water bottle: Hydro Flask 12-Oz. Kids Wide Mouth Bottle
https://assets.bonappetit.com/photos/68c179f28cb212466b3281ff/3:4/w_748%2Cc_limit/Hydro%2520flask%2520kids%2520water%2520bottle.jpg
Hydro Flask Kids Water Bottle - 12 Oz.
AccordionItemContainerButton
Pros
Durable
Dishwasher-safe
Lightweight
Comes in a variety of distinctive colors
Cons
Straw can leak a little eventually

What we love: We were a long-time Yeti family—until I started testing kids' water bottles and was wowed by the Hydro Flask Kids bottle. Like Yeti’s comparable Rambler Jr. kids water bottle, the Hydro Flask kids wide-mouth bottle is a 12-oz. stainless-steel, vacuum-insulated bottle that keeps drinks cold all day. Both have a nearly leakproof flip-down, hard-plastic straw spout, and both can be customized when you order directly from the brand (hot tip: Customizing a kids’ water bottle prevents your pricey purchase from disappearing into the lost and found forever). But empty, the Hydro Flask weighs just 9.5 oz., which is a lot lighter than the 16-oz. Yeti Rambler Jr.

The Hydro Flask has another kid-friendly feature I really appreciate: A removable silicone “boot” that softens the sound of a metal vessel hitting a desk, countertop, or floor. The silicone also makes the bottle less likely to slide off of a surface (though it makes it a little trickier to slide into a backpack sleeve). Ours still looks great after daily trips through the dishwasher too. Over the years straws have disappeared, and my youngest son managed to gnaw the hard plastic spout into something nearly unrecognizable, but another thing this bottle has going for it is that Hydro Flask lids and straws are easy and affordable to replace.
What we'd leave: There's almost nothing not to like about this bottle. The straws will start to leak eventually (if your kid manages not to lose them), but like I said: They're easy to replace.
The best budget insulated kids water bottle: ThermoFlask 16-Oz. Kids Bottle with Straw Lid
https://assets.bonappetit.com/photos/68c17a9173fb36c046de003e/3:4/w_748%2Cc_limit/Thermoflask%2520kids%2520water%2520bottle%252016%2520ounce.jpg
ThermoFlask Kids Bottle with Straw Lid - 16 Oz.
AccordionItemContainerButton
Pros
Affordable
More durable than pricier bottles
Comes as a set of 2 for inevitable replacement
Cons
Insulation not as good as more expensive bottles
No customization or kid-friendly designs

What we love: If you’ve been researching kids water bottles, you’ve probably come across at least a few recommendations for the Takeya kids water bottle. Well, you know what? I hate it. My kids’ Takeya lost its handle and the powder coating started to scrape off in multiple places within a month of normal use. But the much more affordable ThermoFlask water bottle is nearly identical to the Takeya, it’s much more durable, and you can get a two-pack of 16-oz. ThermoFlask bottles for about the same price as one of Takeya’s. If the Hydro Flask feels too expensive for something you know your kids are going to lose anyway, these much more affordable ThermoFlask bottles are a great alternative.

What we'd leave: They don’t keep water ice cold quite as long as a Hydro Flask or Yeti, they’re only available in a few solid colors, and they aren’t customizable, but it’s a great bottle at an accessible price.
The best insulated water bottle for toddlers: 12-Oz. Thermos Funtainer
https://assets.bonappetit.com/photos/68c323301f49a98d0c7f1a1d/3:4/w_748%2Cc_limit/Thermos%2520Funtainer%2520water%2520bottle.jpg
Thermos Funtainer Water Bottle with Straw - 12 Oz.
AccordionItemContainerButton
Pros
Straw easy for very small children to use
Leakproof
Easy to order replacement parts
Cons
Straw requires cleaning with a brush

What we love: Pediatricians generally recommend kids start drinking from a straw before their first birthday, but the hard plastic straw lid on the Hydro Flask kids bottle up above is pretty big—and that bottle is recommended for ages three and up, anyway. So if you’re looking for an insulated water bottle for toddlers, look no further than the Thermos Funtainer. The silicone straw is safe, soft, and small enough for even the tiniest mouths. When the lid is properly closed, it’s leakproof, and the double-walled insulation will keep water cold for up to 12 hours. The hinged handle has grippy silicone for little hands, plus a push-button lid that snaps shut to keep the straw clean (because those little hands can get more than a little grubby and germy as the day goes on).

I also appreciate that this bottle is slim enough to slip into carseat cup holders, lunchboxes, and smaller side pockets on toddler-size backpacks. This bottle comes in a ton of cool colors and designs, and depending on where you buy it, you may even be able to find one with your kiddo’s favorite character on it (hello, Bluey!).

What we'd leave: Though all of the parts are dishwasher safe, you should clean the straw with a straw brush from time to time (more annoying than if you didn't have to do that), and if it gets too gunky you'll have to just order replacements.
The best plastic water bottle for toddlers: Nalgene Kids Sustain Grip-N-Gulp Water Bottle
